The people on the trip came from all walks of life — all kinds of religions, traditions, nationalities and ages. Crespi herself has been to Kailash twice. “Being on that soil, walking on that soil, looking at the faces of those people, those gentle, beautiful people that are there … these are the people that are from the region that support you along the journey,” Crespi said. “It’s heartbreaking because, you know, this is a hugely spiritual part of the world, and to see to see the level of devastation right now, it’s humongous.” There were more than 700 additional travelers with the Isha Foundation and Sadhguru still on the Tibet side when the floods hit, Crespi said. Those people were all safe, and are on their way back to their homes. Since the flooding, Sadhguru hosted an event in Kathmandu called “In Solidarity with Nepal,” calling for nations around the world to support the region, Crespi said. The plan was for this year to be Sadhguru’s last sojourn, but now, he plans to return, Crespi said. “Looking at the scale of destruction, it looks bad,” Sadhguru said in a video message recorded on Aug. 26 and posted to the Isha Foundation’s website. “The same building where we were for immigration just a week ago, that entire building is washed away, and part of the town is washed away.” The guru had tears in his eyes as he choked through the information he had on the group, and the audience behind the camera can be heard weeping. Sadhguru said in the video that he had passed by the group while they were on their way down Mount Kailash and he and his group were on their way up. Sadhguru recieved a message from the group’s guide at 9:05 a.m. that they had arrived at the immigration center, and the floods swept through at 9:14 a.m., he said in the video. The guide had a Nepali phone that would have become active if the group had crossed over into the country, but the phone never came online, Sadhguru said. The first day or two were dedicated to relaying information to families, but now, the reality is sinking in. Crespi is leaning on the yoga and meditation techniques she learned when she first came to the Isha Foundation over 20 years ago, she said, to handle the grief. “Right now for me, I’m recognizing the painful reality of the situation,” Crespi said. “At 42, I learned to meditate, and I have to tell you, it’s been an anchoring thing for me throughout this. It keeps me at a certain level of centeredness and clarity and perception. It doesn’t mean there’s no pain. There’s definitely a deep pain and compassion, but there’s a certain stability that moves you forward, and that has been a godsend.” Contact faith and family editor Kailee Shores at kshores@timesfreepress.com or 423-757-6659.

title: Chinese worker rescued after 10 days trapped in Nepal tunnel - KHGI
description: Chinese worker rescued after 10 days trapped in Nepal tunnel  KHGI
publisher.title: KHGI
full_article:
(TNND) — Ten days after catastrophic flash floods tore through Nepal’s mountains, rescuers pulled a Chinese worker from a mud-filled hydropower tunnel, a rare moment of relief amid a disaster that has killed more than 1,300 people and left thousands unaccounted for.

The flash floods struck Nepal and China’s Tibet region on Aug. 26, likely after a glacier collapse. Nepal’s disaster management agency said nearly 4,900 people remain missing. Earlier in the response, authorities reported more than 3,700 people had been rescued in Nepal.

On the Tibet side of the border, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported 43 deaths and 519 people missing as of Saturday evening. CCTV said 261 of those missing were foreigners.

Rescue operations have focused in part on hydropower sites in Nepal’s Rasuwa district and the devastated Gyirong border crossing in Tibet. Authorities previously believed more than 100 people could be trapped inside a mud-filled tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project.

CCTV reported that Lu Haitao, a 49-year-old Chinese worker, was rescued Saturday from a 225-meter, or roughly 740-foot, hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa, 10 days after the floods. Rescuers carried Lu out of the tunnel and evacuated him by helicopter, according to CCTV, which reported he was hospitalized in stable condition.

Lu told CCTV he had climbed to the highest point in the tunnel and had begun to lose hope before rescue crews found him. CCTV reported Lu is a former farmer from Henan province who also worked as a carpenter, and that he traveled to Nepal in February for his first job abroad.

As the search continues, families of missing people have searched hospitals and relief centers and posted photographs and contact information in hopes of finding relatives.

Rescue work has been complicated by steep mountains, narrow gorges and concern about further flooding from a lake that formed in the Himalayas after the initial disaster. Chinese monitoring data showed the water level in that new lake had dropped about 10 meters, or 32 feet, from its peak.

Nepal said it mobilized domestic and international resources, including an 11-member tunnel-rescue reconnaissance team from India. A similar team from China was expected.

Nepal has received more than 57 metric tons of relief supplies from India, with aid also arriving from China, Japan, Australia and other countries.

नेपाल आरू चीन केरऽ तिब्बत क्षेत्र म॑ २६ अगस्त क॑ आकस्मिक बाढ़ आबी गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरऽ संभावना ग्लेशियर केरऽ गिरला के बाद होय गेलऽ छै । नेपाल के आपदा प्रबंधन एजेंसी के कहनाय छनि जे करीब 4900 लोक लापता अछि. एहि सं पहिने प्रतिक्रिया मे अधिकारी नेपाल मे 3700 सं बेसि लोक के बचाओल गेल अछि.

सीमा के तिब्बत तरफ चीनी सरकारी प्रसारक सीसीटीवी में शनिदिन साँझ तक 43 लोक के मौत आ 519 लोक के लापता होय के खबर अछि. सीसीटीवी के कहनाय अछि जे लापता मे सं 261 गोटे विदेशी छथिन्ह.

बचाव कार्य कुछ हद तक नेपाल केरऽ रसुवा जिला केरऽ जलविद्युत स्थल आरू तिब्बत केरऽ तबाह ग्यरोंग सीमा पार प॑ केंद्रित छै । अधिकारि सब के पहिने विश्वास छल जे अपर त्रिशुली-1 जलविद्युत परियोजना के कीचड़ सं भरल सुरंग के अंदर 100 सं बेसी लोक फंसल भ सकैत अछि.

सीसीटीवी के खबर छै कि बाढ़ के 10 दिन बाद शनिदिन रसुवा के 225 मीटर यानी लगभग 740 फीट के जलविद्युत सुरंग स॑ 49 वर्षीय चीनी मजदूर लु हैताओ क॑ बचाय लेलऽ गेलै । सीसीटीवी के अनुसार बचावकर्मी लु क॑ सुरंग स॑ बाहर निकाली क॑ हेलीकॉप्टर स॑ बाहर निकाली लेलकै, जेकरा म॑ हुनकऽ हालत स्थिर अस्पताल म॑ भर्ती होय के खबर छै ।

लू सीसीटीवी क॑ बतैलकै कि हुनी सुरंग केरऽ सबस॑ ऊँचऽ बिंदु प॑ चढ़ी गेलऽ छै आरू बचाव दल न॑ ओकरा मिलै स॑ पहल॑ ही उम्मीद खोना शुरू करी देल॑ छै । सीसीटीवी केरऽ रिपोर्ट छै कि लु हेनान प्रांत केरऽ पूर्व किसान छै जे बढ़ई के काम भी करै छेलै, आरू वू फरवरी म॑ विदेश म॑ अपनऽ पहिलऽ नौकरी लेली नेपाल गेलऽ छेलै ।

तलाशी जारी रहला पर लापता लोक के परिवार अस्पताल आ राहत केंद्र के तलाशी लेलक आ रिश्तेदार के खोजय के उम्मीद मे फोटो आओर संपर्क जानकारी पोस्ट केलक अछि.

खड़ा पहाड़, संकीर्ण गॉर्ज आरू प्रारंभिक आपदा के बाद हिमालय म॑ बनलऽ झील स॑ आरू बाढ़ के चिंता के कारण बचाव के काम जटिल होय गेलऽ छै । चीनी निगरानी केरऽ आंकड़ा स॑ पता चललै कि पानी केरऽ स्तर ई बात स॑ पता चललै कि नया झील अपनऽ चरम स॑ लगभग १० मीटर यानी ३२ फीट गिरी गेलऽ छै ।

नेपाल भारत सँ ११ सदस्यीय सुरंग-बचाव टोही दल सहित घरेलु आ अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय संसाधन जुटाओल गेल बतौलक अछि । चीन स सेहो एहने टीम क उम्मीद छल।

नेपाल भारत सँ ५७ मीट्रिक टन सँ बेसी राहत सामग्री प्राप्त केलक अछि, चीन, जापान, ऑस्ट्रेलिया आ अन्य देश सँ सेहो सहायता पहुँचल अछि ।

title: Nepal Flood Disaster - Caritas Australia
description: Nepal Flood Disaster  Caritas Australia
publisher.title: Caritas Australia
full_article:
The full scale of the disaster is continuing to emerge. Hundreds of people have been killed and thousands are missing. Entire communities have been destroyed, roads and bridges have been washed away, and thousands of families have been displaced.

The disaster was triggered by a massive flood surge through the Bhote Koshi River on 26 August, devastating communities across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and other downstream districts. Rescue operations remain underway, but damaged infrastructure and ongoing flood risks continue to limit access to many affected communities.

The humanitarian needs remain immense. Families urgently require food, clean water, shelter, health care and essential household items. Schools and health facilities have also been damaged, and humanitarian assessments indicate that thousands of children need support.

ई आपदा 26 अगस्त क॑ भोटे कोशी नदी के माध्यम स॑ भारी बाढ़ के लहर स॑ शुरू होय गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा स॑ पूरा रसुवा, नुवाकोट, धडिंग आरू अन्य डाउनस्ट्रीम जिला के समुदाय तबाह होय गेलऽ छेलै । बचाव अभियान जारी छै, लेकिन क्षतिग्रस्त बुनियादी ढाँचा आरू जारी बाढ़ के जोखिम के कारण बहुत प्रभावित समुदायऽ तलक पहुँच सीमित होय रहलऽ छै ।

मानवीय आवश्यकता अपार बनल अछि। परिवारक कें तत्काल भोजन, स्वच्छ पानी, आवास, स्वास्थ्य देखभाल आ आवश्यक घरेलू सामान कें आवश्यकता होयत छै. स्कूल आ स्वास्थ्य सुविधाक कें सेहो नुकसान पहुंचल छै, आ मानवीय आकलन सं पता चलय छै कि हजारक बच्चाक कें सहायता कें जरूरत छै.

title: Connecticut’s Nepali community holds vigil for flood victims - wfsb.com
description: Connecticut’s Nepali community holds vigil for flood victims  wfsb.com
publisher.title: wfsb.com
full_article:
WEST HARTFORD, Conn. (WFSB) - Connecticut’s Nepali community gathered Sunday evening at West Hartford Town Hall for a candlelight vigil honoring those killed and missing after flash floods in Nepal’s Bhote Koshi Valley.

Dozens attended the vigil, and organizers said the gathering was meant to remember those who lost their lives and to support families still waiting for answers.

Families await word from Nepal

Many families in Connecticut’s Nepali community have relatives and friends in the areas hit by the floods, and some are still waiting to hear from loved ones.

As of Sept. 3, Nepal’s disaster authority reported about 1,252 people dead and more than 4,200 people still missing.

Vigil draws young and old

Those gathered said they are holding on to hope and doing what they can to support those affected back home.

Bishesh Pariyar, 8, said, “I just feel sad, worried about all my family stuck in Nepal with the flood.”

Kashbi Kandel, 14, said, “We’re sending prayers for them, hoping their okay and everything will be okay and we will move past this.”

title: Bangladesh sought more energy from Nepal, but floods have halted exports - Eco-Business
description: Bangladesh sought more energy from Nepal, but floods have halted exports  Eco-Business
publisher.title: Eco-Business
full_article:
Monsoon rains have routinely given Nepal a surge of hydropower, creating a surplus. Some of that surplus was used to supplement downstream neighbour Bangladesh’s fossil-fuel-dependent electricity supply.

On 26 August, however, Nepal’s hydropower system was damaged extensively. Flash floods swept through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems, killing at least 1,250 people as of 3 September. The floods also damaged 15 hydropower plants and critical transmission infrastructure, wiping out over 750 MW of electricity generation, reported Time. Nearly 900 hydropower workers are missing.

The disaster has now disrupted Nepal’s electricity exports, with supplies to Bangladesh halted, authorities in Dhaka and Kathmandu confirmed to Dialogue Earth.

On 3 September, Shaligram Bhandari, a spokesperson for Nepal’s Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, told Dialogue Earth that floods damaged the 22 megawatt (MW) Chilime and 24 MW Trishuli hydropower projects, which have since stopped generating electricity. The power they produced had been approved for export to Bangladesh. Nepal halted all power exports, Reuters reported several days earlier.

Amid the disaster, the ministry had yet to explore alternatives, Bhandari said.

Nepal’s growing role as a hydropower exporter must be viewed together with these vulnerabilities.

“ Hydropower from Nepal and Bhutan could provide Bangladesh with a cheaper source of electricity than many of the country’s existing generation sources. Shafiqul Alam, lead analyst for Bangladesh, Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis

Complicating its role as an exporter is its lack of a shared border with Bangladesh. Electricity trade between them has passed through India’s transmission network, which comes with some conditions.

Since 2024, Nepal has been exporting 40 MW of electricity to Bangladesh through India’s network every June to November. It wanted to export 20 MW more. But this June, the Indian power trading company which manages cross-border grid operations with Bangladesh declined the request, Nepali government officials told the Kathmandu Post. The company, NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Limited, reportedly cited capacity constraints on the India-Bangladesh transmission line.

In July, India held energy cooperation talks with Nepal. While there was development on bilateral energy coordination, there was no resolution on the 20 MW issue.

That amount is minuscule compared to the size of the three countries’ electricity grids, which have a combined total installed capacity of around 586 GW. But energy experts, officials and power-sector analysts in those countries told Dialogue Earth the 20 MW impasse is more nuanced than it appears. There are technical, procedural and political factors at play, they note.

The disruption in Nepal comes at a particularly difficult time for Bangladesh, which has experienced severe load-shedding in recent days. It faced a power shortfall exceeding 3,500 MW at one point, as well as widespread outages across the country. The loss of electricity from Nepal only adds to that pressure.

While Bangladeshi and Nepali experts point to unused capacity on the India-Bangladesh transmission link, Indian experts say there could be a genuine capacity limitation on the line. In the absence of a regional body and trade mechanism dedicated to energy, procedural lapses and politics also have major roles to play, they note. Strained India-Bangladesh relations since Bangladesh’s 2024 change of government may also be involved.

Why Bangladesh wants Nepal’s hydropower

Nepal and Bangladesh have complementary electricity needs. The summer monsoon gives Nepal surplus hydropower, which Bangladesh can use to diversify its energy sources. In the dry winter, these roles reverse somewhat – Nepal faces shortages while Bangladesh’s demand dips – making cross-border trade beneficial in both directions over the year.

In 2025-2026, Nepal’s total installed capacity reached 4.1 GW, but monthly peak domestic demand stood at only around 2.5 GW, according to the Nepal Energy Authority. Electricity exports bring total demand up to about 3.2 GW.

Bangladesh has 32 GW of installed power generation capacity, 98 per cent of which is dependent on fossil fuels, according to energy think-tank Ember. The country wants to diversify sources to meet its current demand. Bangladesh also aims to cover 20 per cent of its electricity needs from non-imported renewables by 2030. Energy trade between Nepal and Bangladesh therefore makes “economic sense”, says Shahriar Ahmed Chowdhury, director of the Centre for Energy Research at United International University in Dhaka. “Hydropower from Nepal and Bhutan could provide Bangladesh with a cheaper source of electricity than many of the country’s existing generation sources,” says Shafiqul Alam, lead analyst for Bangladesh energy at the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis. “Ideally, electricity trade should work both ways,” Chowdhury says. But expanding such trade is “a political decision”, he notes. “The volume is small, but it is important because it marks the beginning of cross-border electricity cooperation.” Cross-border electricity trade helps Bangladesh primarily by shielding it from geopolitical disruptions to energy supplies, volatility in international fuel prices and diversification, experts say. After all, the additional 20 MW will not help Bangladesh meet its 20 per cent renewables target. There is no plan to include imports within what is a domestic generation target, says Aninda Islam Amit, Bangladesh’s state minister for power, energy and mineral resources. He expects the country’s private sector to “take the lead” on renewables as there are “incentives for private entrepreneurs”, he tells Dialogue Earth. For Nepal, the energy trade is part of a much larger ambition. During the July energy talks, it agreed to increase its export capacity as India ups its import capacity. Nepali energy minister Birajbhakta Shrestha tells Dialogue Earth that the deal is another step towards fulfilling the country’s agreement to export 10 GW of electricity to India, signed in 2024. A Nepali energy ministry official, requesting anonymity, says the immediate 20-MW issue could be resolved through trilateral discussions between Nepal, India and Bangladesh. India holds the missing link The 40 MW Nepal currently exports to Bangladesh is transported by the Baharampur-Bheramara high-voltage DC interconnection from east India, where it arrives on a transmission line from southern Nepal. The Baharampur-Bheramara link between India and Bangladesh has a transfer capacity of 1 GW. The country typically receives around 920-930 MW through the link, leaving some unused transfer capacity, said a Bangladesh Power Division official speaking on condition of anonymity. Nepal has also been considering alternatives. “If power cannot be exported via the Baharampur-Bheramara line, there is option for Nepal to export the additional 20 MW through other Indian transmission lines connected to Bangladesh,” says Manoj Silwal, former deputy managing director of the Nepal Electricity Authority. Apart from the Baharampur-Bheramara link, Bangladesh also imports nearly 1.7 GW from India: 160 MW through the Surajmaninagar to Comilla interconnection, and 1.5 GW from Godda to Rohanpur, the latter operated by Adani Power. However, transporting the 20 MW via existing corridors may not be feasible for a few reasons, says Nikit Abhyankar, an energy efficiency expert at the University of California, Berkeley. It is possible that these corridors are fully utilised. Additionally, the average amount of electricity a transmission line carries is not necessarily the capacity that is safely available, Abhyankar notes. At times of peak demand, power flows can be much higher, and some capacity must be reserved to manage unexpected failures elsewhere in the system. “I would be very surprised if they are actually going to operate a 1,000 MW line at 1,000 MW capacity,” Abhyankar says. A line may also be unable to deliver its rated amount of electricity due to losses from transfers. In a high-voltage DC connection, such as Baharampur-Bheramara, some electricity is lost when power is converted from AC to DC, as it travels along the transmission line, and when converted back to AC at the receiving end. Abhyankar estimates that roughly 40-50 MW could be lost on a 1-GW line. The Baharampur-Bheramara corridor is also loaded with India’s own exports to Bangladesh. India’s Central Electricity Authority “doesn’t want to run the line close to its thermal limit … on a line that also carries India’s own bilateral exports”, notes Binit Das, deputy programme manager for renewable energy at the Centre for Science and Environment (CSE). For the India-Bangladesh link, battery storage could potentially help if the line has spare capacity during periods of lower demand, Abhyankar adds. But feasibility depends on how much the power flow on the interconnection varies over the day. Politics complicates power trade Geography presents India with an unavoidable role in any future Nepal-Bangladesh electricity trade. “There is no other way that Bangladesh can get power from either Nepal or Bhutan without that being facilitated by India,” says Bipul Chattopadhyay, executive director of the Consumer Unity & Trust Society (CUTS), India. Experts see this 20 MW episode as a litmus test for how India prioritises capacity across competing uses of a shared asset. During this impasse, India and Nepal separately reached a much bigger capacity decision: to raise Nepal’s export quota from 1.1 GW to 1.65 GW. “The asymmetry between how quickly that bilateral decision happened and how long the trilateral 20 MW has languished is itself the clearest evidence of where the region’s integration problem actually sits,” says Das of the CSE. India’s role in Nepal’s hydropower sector also complicates the picture. Several Indian companies are developing major hydropower projects in Nepal, while India is also Nepal’s principal electricity export market and the transit country for its exports to Bangladesh. India could increasingly draw on Nepal’s hydropower to meet its own rising demand, Chattopadhyay says. The challenge is to develop a framework that works for all the countries involved. “It should be win-win for all three parties,” he says. “That model is not difficult to develop, but that is something which is still missing in our current political-economic discourse.” He also raises political considerations in the 20-MW denial. Relations between India and Bangladesh have been strained since former prime minister of Bangladesh, Sheikh Hasina, went into exile in India in August 2024, where she remains. “After the change in government in Bangladesh, [the] India-Bangladesh relationship is yet to get on the right track … it’s very frosty,” notes Chattopadhyay. A South Asian electricity market? The difficulty of moving a mere 20 MW points to bottlenecks in cross-border energy trade in a region with growing energy needs. Every prior expansion of the transmission corridor, including the original 40 MW, was formalised through a Joint Steering Committee (JSC) decision followed by a tripartite agreement. The 13th Nepal-India JSC meeting was held in July, having last convened in February 2025, but failed to yield success with the 20 MW addition. There is also a broader institutional problem. Cross-border electricity trade between Bangladesh, Bhutan and Nepal, where it goes through India, requires multiple layers of approval. This includes a tripartite power sale agreement, clearance from India’s Central Electricity Authority and a JSC to anchor the decision. Over the last few years, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Nepal have signed bilateral agreements with India to develop electricity trade. As of April, India has entered into 17 power-sector agreements with neighbouring countries. It is also involved in 13 cross-border power-generation projects and 30 transmission-link projects. Trilateral and regional transactions carry a layer of political and procedural friction that bilateral ones don’t, Das says. This makes the region’s power systems interconnected yet fragmented. The potential benefits of deeper integration are significant. Cross-border electricity trade can allow these countries to complement one another’s demands, reducing reliance on fossil fuels while improving energy security and lowering costs, joint research by CUTS and Chintan Research Foundation found. The stakes are also different for countries of different sizes. “For a large system like India … small cross-border trade doesn’t really make a huge difference. But for countries like Nepal to sell their hydroelectricity [and] for countries like Bangladesh to meet their electricity demand reliably, cross-border trade becomes important,” says Abhyankar. Yet there is still no subregional institution focused on coordinating and facilitating cross-border electricity trade. A regional power exchange, an agreed open-access framework, or institutionalised, calendar-bound trilateral bodies could provide a more predictable way of handling third-country transit, says Das. “Without such a mechanism, episodes like the 20-MW holdup could continue to recur even as the region’s growing hydropower surplus and complementary electricity demand make the case for trade increasingly obvious,” he says. परिवहन किछ कारण सं संभव नहिं भ सकैत अछि. संभव अछि जे एहि गलियारा क पूर्ण उपयोग होए। एकरऽ अलावा, एक ट्रांसमिशन लाइन म॑ औसतन बिजली के मात्रा जरूरी नै छै कि वू क्षमता सुरक्षित रूप स॑ उपलब्ध होय, अभ्यंकर न॑ नोट करलकै । पीक डिमांड कें समय बिजली कें प्रवाह बहुत बेसि भ सकय छै, आ सिस्टम मे अन्य जगहक पर अप्रत्याशित विफलता कें प्रबंधन कें लेल किच्छू क्षमता आरक्षित करनाय आवश्यक छै. अभिनकर कहैत छथि जे अगर ओ वास्तव मे 1000 मेगावाट क क्षमता पर 1000 मेगावाट क लाइन चलाबए जा रहल छथि त हमरा बहुत आश्चर्य होएत। कोनों लाइन ट्रांसफर सं नुकसान कें कारण अपन रेटेड राशि कें बिजली सेहो नहि पहुंचा सकय छै. हाई-वोल्टेज डीसी कनेक्शन, जेना कि बहारमपुर-भेरामरा मे, जखन बिजली कें एसी सं डीसी मे बदलल जायत छै, कियाकि इ ट्रांसमिशन लाइन कें साथ चलै छै, आ जखन रिसीविंग एंड पर वापस एसी मे बदलल जायत छै, तखन किछ बिजली कें नुकसान भ जायत छै. अभिनकर क अनुमान अछि जे 1 जीडब्ल्यू लाइन पर मोटा-मोटी 40-50 मेगावाट क नुकसान भ सकैत अछि। बहारमपुर-भेरामारा गलियारा भी भारत केरऽ खुद केरऽ बंगलादेश केरऽ निर्यात स॑ भरलऽ छै । भारत केरऽ केंद्रीय बिजली प्राधिकरण “अपनऽ तापीय सीमा के करीब लाइन क॑ नै चलाबै चाहै छै ... ऐन्हऽ लाइन प॑ जे भारत केरऽ अपनऽ द्विपक्षीय निर्यात भी ले जाय छै”, सेंटर फॉर साइंस एंड एनवायरनमेंट (सीएसई) केरऽ अक्षय ऊर्जा केरऽ डिप्टी प्रोग्राम मैनेजर बिनित दास न॑ नोट करलकै । अभिनकर आरू कहै छै कि भारत-बांग्लादेश लिंक लेली बैटरी स्टोरेज संभावित रूप स॑ मदद करी सकै छै अगर कम मांग के दौरान लाइन म॑ स्पेयर क्षमता छै । मुदा व्यवहार्यता एहि बात पर निर्भर करैत अछि जे इंटरकनेक्टेशन पर बिजलीक प्रवाह दिन भरि कतेक बदलैत रहैत अछि । राजनीति बिजली व्यापार के जटिल बनाबै छै भूगोल भारत के सामने कोनो भी भविष्य के नेपाल-बांग्लादेश विद्युत व्यापार में अपरिहार्य भूमिका के सामने पेश करै छै । भारत केरऽ कंज्यूमर यूनिटी एंड ट्रस्ट सोसाइटी (सीयूटीएस) केरऽ कार्यकारी निदेशक बिपुल चट्टोपाध्याय न॑ कहलकै कि भारत केरऽ सहायता के बिना बंगलादेश क॑ नेपाल या भूटान स॑ बिजली मिलै के दोसरऽ तरीका नै छै । विशेषज्ञ ई 20 मेगावाट केरऽ एपिसोड क॑ ई बात लेली लिटमस टेस्ट के रूप म॑ देखै छै कि भारत साझा संपत्ति केरऽ प्रतिस्पर्धी उपयोगऽ म॑ क्षमता क॑ कोना प्राथमिकता दै छै । एहि गतिरोध के दौरान भारत आ नेपाल अलग-अलग बहुत पैघ क्षमता वाला निर्णय पर पहुंचल छल जे नेपाल के निर्यात कोटा के 1.1 जीडब्ल्यू सं बढ़ा क 1.65 जीडब्ल्यू क देल जाए. सीएसई केरऽ दास न॑ कहलकै कि वू द्विपक्षीय फैसला कतनी जल्दी होय गेलै आरू त्रिपक्षीय २० मेगावाट कतनी देर स॑ सुस्त रहलऽ छै, ई बात के बीच के विषमता ही ई सबस॑ स्पष्ट सबूत छै कि ई क्षेत्र केरऽ एकीकरण के समस्या वास्तव म॑ कत॑ बैठलऽ छै । नेपाल के जलविद्युत क्षेत्र मे भारत के भूमिका सेहो तस्वीर के जटिल बना दैत अछि. नेपाल म॑ कईएक भारतीय कंपनी बड़ऽ जलविद्युत परियोजना विकसित करी रहलऽ छै, जबकि भारत नेपाल केरऽ प्रमुख बिजली निर्यात बाजार आरू बांग्लादेश म॑ निर्यात केरऽ पारगमन देश भी छै । चट्टोपाध्याय के कहनाय छनि जे भारत अपन बढ़ैत मांग के पूरा करय लेल नेपाल के जलविद्युत के तेजी सं फायदा उठा सकैत अछि. चुनौती इ छै कि एकटा एहन रूपरेखा तैयार कैल जै जे एहि मे शामिल सबटा देशक कें लेल काज करय. ओ कहैत छथि जे तीनू पार्टी कए इ जीत-जीत हेबाक चाही। “ओ मॉडल क॑ विकसित करना मुश्किल नै छै, लेकिन वू एगो ऐसनऽ चीज छै जे हमरऽ वर्तमान राजनीतिक-आर्थिक प्रवचन म॑ अखनी भी गायब छै।” ओ 20 मेगावाट क इनकार मे राजनीतिक विचार सेहो उठबैत छथि। अगस्त २०२४ म॑ बांग्लादेश केरऽ पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री शेख हसीना भारत म॑ निर्वासन होय ​​गेलऽ छेलै, तब॑ स॑ भारत आरू बांग्लादेश के बीच संबंध तनावपूर्ण छै, जहां हुनी अखनी भी छै । चट्टोपाध्याय नोट करै छै, “बंग्लादेश म॑ सरकार म॑ बदलाव के बाद [भारत-बांग्लादेश केरऽ] संबंध अभी सही रास्ता प॑ नै आबी सकलऽ छै ... ई बहुत ठंढा छै । दक्षिण एशियाई बिजली बाजार? महज 20 मेगावाट कें स्थानांतरित करय कें कठिनाई ऊर्जा कें जरूरत बढ़य वाला क्षेत्र मे सीमा पार सं ऊर्जा व्यापार मे अड़चन कें ओर इशारा करय छै. मूल 40 मेगावाट सहित संचरण गलियारा केरऽ हर पूर्व विस्तार क॑ संयुक्त संचालन समिति (जेएससी) केरऽ फैसला के माध्यम स॑ औपचारिक रूप देलऽ गेलऽ छेलै आरू ओकरऽ बाद त्रिपक्षीय समझौता करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । नेपाल-भारत जेएससीके १३म बैसार जुलाईमे भेल छल, जे अन्तिम बेर फरवरी २०२५मे बजाओल गेल छल, मुदा २० मेगावाटके जोडलासँ सफलता नहि भेट सकल । एकटा व्यापक संस्थागत समस्या सेहो अछि। बांग्लादेश, भूटान आरू नेपाल के बीच सीमा पार स॑ बिजली के व्यापार, जहां ई भारत स॑ गुजरै छै, ओकरा लेली कई परतऽ के मंजूरी के जरूरत छै । एहि मे त्रिपक्षीय बिजली बिक्री समझौता, भारत क केंद्रीय बिजली प्राधिकरण स मंजूरी आ एहि फैसला कए लंगर लगेबा लेल जेएससी शामिल अछि। पिछला किछु साल स बांग्लादेश, भूटान आ नेपाल भारत क संग बिजली व्यापार क विकास लेल द्विपक्षीय समझौता पर हस्ताक्षर केलक अछि। अप्रैल तक भारत पड़ोसी देशक संग 17 बिजली क्षेत्रक समझौता कएने अछि। इ सीमा पार सं 13 बिजली उत्पादन परियोजना आ 30 संचरण-लिंक परियोजना मे सेहो शामिल छै. दास कहैत छथि जे त्रिपक्षीय आ क्षेत्रीय लेनदेन मे राजनीतिक आ प्रक्रियात्मक घर्षण क परत होइत अछि जे द्विपक्षीय लेनदेन मे नहि होइत अछि । एहि सं एहि क्षेत्र के बिजली प्रणाली एक दोसरा सं जुड़ल अछि मुदा खंडित भ गेल अछि. गहन एकीकरण कें संभावित लाभ महत्वपूर्ण छै. सीयूटीएस आरू चिंतन रिसर्च फाउंडेशन केरऽ संयुक्त शोध म॑ पता चललै कि सीमा पार स॑ बिजली व्यापार ई देशऽ क॑ एक-दूसरा के मांग के पूरक बनाबै के अनुमति द॑ सकै छै, जेकरा स॑ जीवाश्म ईंधन प॑ निर्भरता कम होय सकै छै जबकि ऊर्जा सुरक्षा म॑ सुधार आरू लागत म॑ कमी ​​आबै छै । अलग-अलग आकार के देश के लेल सेहो दांव अलग-अलग अछि. अभिनकर कहै छै, "भारत जैसनऽ बड़ऽ सिस्टम लेली ... सीमा पार स॑ छोटऽ व्यापार स॑ वास्तव म॑ बहुत बड़ऽ फर्क नै पड़ै छै ।लेकिन नेपाल जैसनऽ देश लेली अपनऽ जलविद्युत बेचै लेली [आरू] बांग्लादेश जैसनऽ देश लेली अपनऽ बिजली के मांग क॑ भरोसेमंद तरीका स॑ पूरा करै लेली सीमा पार स॑ व्यापार महत्वपूर्ण होय जाय छै । तइयो एखन धरि कोनो उपक्षेत्रीय संस्था नहि अछि जे सीमा पार सं बिजली व्यापार के समन्वय आ सुविधा देबय पर केंद्रित अछि. दास के कहना छै कि क्षेत्रीय बिजली आदान-प्रदान, सहमत खुला पहुँच ढाँचा या संस्थागत, कैलेंडर स॑ जुड़लऽ त्रिपक्षीय निकाय तेसरऽ देशऽ के पारगमन क॑ संभाल॑ के अधिक पूर्वानुमानित तरीका उपलब्ध करै सकै छै । हुनी कहै छै, “बिना ऐसनौ तंत्र के 20 मेगावाट के होल्डअप जैसनऽ एपिसोड दोबारा आबी सकै छै, भले ही क्षेत्र केरऽ बढ़तऽ जलविद्युत अधिशेष आरू पूरक बिजली के मांग व्यापार केरऽ मामला क॑ तेजी स॑ स्पष्ट करी दै छै । ई लेख मूल रूप स॑ डायलॉग अर्थ प॑ क्रिएटिव कॉमन्स लाइसेंस के तहत प्रकाशित करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

title: Video showing Chinese survivor’s rescue in Nepal released - Korea JoongAng Daily
description: Video showing Chinese survivor’s rescue in Nepal released  Korea JoongAng Daily
publisher.title: Korea JoongAng Daily
full_article:
Video footage showing the tense moment when the Korea Disaster Relief Team (KDRT) rescued a Chinese survivor of the Nepal flash flood was released by Korean authorities on Sunday.

“Are you okay?” a Korean rescuer asked as they pointed the flashlight toward what appeared to be a human figure.

As Korean rescuers approached closer, they confirmed the survivor was waiting on a platform above the flood debris inside the tunnel.

Related Article Far from home, Nepali students in Korea grapple with tragedy of flood

Chinese ambassador thanks Korean rescuers after survivor found in Nepal floods

With the rescuers' instructions and assistance, the survivor climbed down from the platform on his own using an attached metal beam.

The survivor was wearing a full-sleeve T-shirt and only boxer shorts. He was not wearing shoes.

“When the rescuers’ light shone on me, I could not shout back because I could not believe that they were here to save me,” the survivor told Chinese broadcaster CCTV.

A Chinese survivor trapped inside a tunnel smiles as Korean rescuers come to save him in footage carried by Yonhap News TV. KOREA DISASTER RELIEF TEAM

The footage was recorded with a camera attached to the Korean rescuers' helmets. The clip also showed the rescuers wading through mud that reached their upper torsos.

The Chinese survivor was found inside a 225-meter-long (738-foot-long) tunnel and was later transported to a military hospital by helicopter.

The survivor was found at the hydropower plant construction site where the nine missing Koreans had been working. One Korean is believed to be near the weir dam, close to where the survivor was found, while the other eight are believed to be farther downstream.

The KDRT plans to continue the search mission inside the tunnel, as the survivor said another person was nearby, though he did not know whether the person was alive.

Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun is also set to hold ministerial talks with his Nepali counterpart regarding rescue efforts to find missing Koreans.





BY LEE SOO-JUNG [lee.soojung1@joongang.co.kr]
translated:
कोरिया आपदा राहत दल (केडीआरटी) न॑ नेपाल केरऽ झटका बाढ़ स॑ बची क॑ निकललऽ चीनी आदमी क॑ बचाबै के तनावपूर्ण क्षण क॑ देखाबै वाला वीडियो फुटेज रविवार क॑ कोरियाई अधिकारियऽ न॑ जारी करलकै ।

“अहाँ ठीक छी?” एकटा कोरियाई बचावकर्ता टॉर्च के ओहि दिस इशारा करैत पुछलकै जे मनुक्खक आकृति बुझाइत छल.

कोरियाई बचावकर्ता सब जेना-जेना नजदीक आबि रहल छल, ओ सब पुष्टि केलक जे बचि गेल आदमी सुरंग के अंदर बाढ़ के मलबा के ऊपर एकटा प्लेटफार्म पर इंतजार क रहल छल।

संबंधित लेख घर स दूर कोरिया मे नेपाली छात्र बाढ़िक त्रासदी स जूझैत छथि

नेपाल में बाढ़ि के 12 दिन बाद एखनो लापता 9 कोरियाई के खोज में चीनी बचि गेल चीनी के बचाओल गेल

नेपालक बाढ़िमे बचि गेल व्यक्ति भेटलाक बाद कोरियाई उद्धारकके धन्यवाद दैत चीनी राजदूत

लापता कोरियाई के खोज, अन्य बाढ़ के मुद्दा पर मन्त्री वार्ता के लेल विदेश मन्त्री नेपाल जेताह

बचावकर्मी के निर्देश आरू सहायता स॑ बची गेलऽ आदमी संलग्न धातु के बीम के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ अपनऽ दम प॑ प्लेटफार्म स॑ नीचें चढ़ी गेलै ।

बचि गेल व्यक्ति फुल स्लीव टी-शर्ट आ केवल बॉक्सर शॉर्ट्स पहिरने छल। जूता नहि पहिरने छलाह।

चीनी प्रसारक सीसीटीवी स बचि गेल व्यक्ति कहला जे जखन बचावकर्मी क इजोत हमरा पर चमकल त हम वापस चिचिया नहि सकलहुं, किया कि हमरा विश्वास नहि भ रहल छल जे ओ हमरा बचाबय लेल एतय आयल छथि।

सुरंग के भीतर फंसलऽ एगो चीनी बची गेलऽ आदमी मुस्कुराबै छै जब॑ कोरियाई बचावकर्मी ओकरा बचाबै लेली आबै छै, जेकरा म॑ योनहाप न्यूज टीवी द्वारा देलऽ गेलऽ फुटेज छै । कोरिया आपदा राहत टीम

चीनी बची गेलऽ ई व्यक्ति क॑ २२५ मीटर (७३८ फीट लंबा) सुरंग के भीतर मिललै आरू बाद म॑ ओकरा हेलीकॉप्टर स॑ सैन्य अस्पताल पहुँचैलऽ गेलै ।

बचि गेल व्यक्ति जलविद्युत संयंत्र निर्माण स्थल पर भेटल जतय नौ टा लापता कोरियाई काज क रहल छल। मानल जा रहल अछि जे एकटा कोरियाई वेयर डैम के पास अछि, जतय सं बचल बच्चा भेटल छल, ओकर नजदीक अछि, जखन कि बाकी आठ गोटे के बारे में मानल जा रहल अछि जे ओ बेसी नीचा अछि.

केडीआरटी केरऽ योजना छै कि सुरंग के भीतर खोज मिशन जारी रखलऽ जाय, कैन्हेंकि बची गेलऽ आदमी न॑ कहलकै कि पास म॑ एगो आरू व्यक्ति छै, हालांकि ओकरा ई पता नै छेलै कि वू व्यक्ति जीवित छै कि नै ।

कोरिया केरऽ विदेश मंत्री चो ह्यून न॑ भी लापता कोरियाई लोगऽ क॑ खोजै के बचाव के प्रयास के संबंध म॑ अपनऽ नेपाली समकक्ष के साथ मन्त्री वार्ता करै वाला छै ।

title: Nepali community rallies for flood victims in West Hartford - NBC Connecticut
description: Nepali community rallies for flood victims in West Hartford  NBC Connecticut
publisher.title: NBC Connecticut
full_article:
The Nepali community gathered Sunday in West Hartford to mourn the victims of devastating floods in Nepal and raise money for relief efforts more than a week after the disaster.

More than 1,300 people have died and more than 5,000 remain missing across Nepal and China after flooding that was likely triggered by a glacier collapse.

Stream Connecticut News for free, 24/7, wherever you are. WATCH HERE

In West Hartford, community members lit candles and arranged them around the flag of Nepal during a vigil for those affected by the disaster.

“We’re sending prayers and hoping they’re okay,” 14-year-old Kashvi Kandeo of West Hartford said.

The flooding swept away buildings and people, leaving members of Connecticut’s Nepali community struggling to comprehend videos showing the destruction.

“It really hurts to see your home country get destroyed like this,” Kandeo said.

That shock has also prompted the community to take action. The vigil brought together members of the Nepali community as well as local and state leaders while raising money for relief efforts.

Local South Windsor 3 hours ago Crews search for missing male after jet ski accident West Haven 10 hours ago Suspect bit police K-9 while being apprehended by officers in West Haven: police

“Whenever these things happen, the whole community comes together and want to gather and try to support it,” West Hartford resident Pramod Pradhan said.

West Hartford is home to one of Connecticut’s largest Nepali communities, with about 1,000 Nepali people living in Hartford County, based on data compiled by the Asian and Asian American Studies Institute at UConn.

Vigil organizers said they have collectively raised a few thousand dollars to support relief efforts.

Community members said the disaster has also demonstrated the resilience of the Nepali people.

“They’re really strong for that because so much has happened and the fact that they can keep pushing forward it just really shows how strong they are,” Kandeo said.

Organizers in West Hartford are asking people who want to contribute to relief efforts in Nepal to donate directly to the Nepalese government. That can be found here.

title: A local woman is finding ways to help family and community back in Nepal - kimt.com
description: A local woman is finding ways to help family and community back in Nepal  kimt.com
publisher.title: kimt.com
full_article:
MINNEAPOLIS (WCCO) -- For Jeena Gurung Vomhof, the Minnesota State Fair was supposed to be a celebration.

A chance to share the art and traditions of the country she still calls home.

Then came devastating news from Nepal.

"I was almost done with the set up to be selling at the 2026 Minnesota State Fair. Excited, pumped, you know, new space, new energy, and I couldn't, I couldn't see my social media, like what's happening. It was like, that was not real to me. And I just called my mom and said what's happening," said Gurung Vomhof.

Gurung Vomhof is originally from Kathmandu.

Nepal is home to Gurung Vomhof's family, her memories, and the women whose work she brings to Minnesota.

"Nepal is a beautiful country. It's an Asian country, right below China and above India, surrounded by beautiful mountains, beautiful people, the tradition, the culture, the love, the humanity that is there in the country I still miss and I try to bring that wherever I go," explained Gurung Vomhof.

Through her business, Namaste Brows & Boutique in Roseville, Gurung Vomhof employs sixteen women in Nepalmaking — hand-crafted earrings, cashmere shawls, hemp, and felt gift items. 100% of the proceeds go back to the makers.

"Each and every piece that I sell has a story," said Gurung Vomhof.

But right now, she's carrying a story of loss.

"My friends, my family, who are far and close, are still back home and we have lost two cousins, 21 and 35, who were going trekking. They're missing," said Gurung Vomhof.

She talks with family every day, trying to stay connected while holding herself together.

At the fair, people she doesn't know are giving her something she needs right now.

"My favorite thing right now is hugs. You know, when I'm holding all of this, I don't know how, I have the right word physically, emotionally. Joy, hurt? That hug means so much," said Gurung Vomhof

Those moments are helping her keep going.

She's already thinking beyond the immediate crisis - about children, education, and rebuilding.

"Education is the root of everything, everything. For me, maybe I can build a classroom, but I can't do it alone. I need all of you," said Gurung Vomhof.

For now, she'll keep standing for Nepal, sharing its culture, and believing in the people standing with her.

"I am at the grandstand at the lower level, row number nine, wide open with colors, with joy, and I'm going to be standing here every single minute," said Gurung Vomhof.

title: Monday Starter: Nun leading Caritas Nepal calls for international aid after floods - Global Sisters Report
description: Monday Starter: Nun leading Caritas Nepal calls for international aid after floods  Global Sisters Report
publisher.title: Global Sisters Report
full_article:
With the death toll mounting to more than 1,000 and with more than 4,500 missing, the executive director of Caritas Nepal is warning that the disaster caused by massive flooding in the country on Aug. 26 has not fully played out and will require international support for months to come. "The situation remains extremely alarming, and the number of casualties continues to rise as search and rescue operations are still ongoing," Sr. Cecilia Durga Shrestha, a member of the Sisters of St. Joseph of Cluny and head of Caritas Nepal since 2023, said of Nepal government search, rescue and relief efforts. "Thousands of people have been affected, with many lives lost, people still missing, and significant damage to homes, roads, bridges, livelihoods and other essential infrastructure," Shrestha told GSR, speaking specifically of the flooding that swept through communities in Nuwakot near the Himalayan nation's border with China.

Sr. Cecilia Durga Shrestha, a member of the Sisters of St. Joseph of Cluny, has been serving as executive director of Caritas Nepal since 2023. (Courtesy of Caritas Nepal)

Shrestha said that since the second day of the disaster, Caritas Nepal and its partners have been on the ground accompanying affected communities. "We are providing food and non-food items, essential household utensils, and other emergency supplies," Shrestha said. "We are also supporting people who have lost family members with essential items needed for mourning and funeral rituals, as well as providing medical kits to affected communities in different locations." However, at present, the most urgent needs include temporary shelter, debris clearance, essential household items, temporary learning centers for children, psychosocial counseling, medical assistance and support to restore basic livelihoods and services. Shrestha stressed the need for the international community to continue accompanying affected communities in the coming months. "Financial support would be particularly valuable to enable us to respond to both immediate humanitarian needs and the longer-term recovery and rebuilding of affected families and communities," she said. Nepal has a population of 31 million and is predominantly Hindu, with only about 10,000 Roman Catholics. But Caritas' response, Shrestha said, is to extend a "helping hand to the affected people from the ground," regardless of religious affiliation.

Loyola University honors the late Sr. Jean Schmidt with campus statue Loyola University Chicago has honored one of its icons, the late Sr. Jean Dolores Schmidt — longtime Loyola Ramblers basketball fan, team chaplain and campus fixture — with a statue on the university's Rogers Park campus. The Aug. 21 unveiling of the cast bronze statue, which depicts Schmidt sitting on a bench and holding a Loyola basketball, fell on what would have been the beloved sister's 107th birthday and a little less than a year since Schmidt's death at age 106 on Oct. 9, 2025. Known to all as Sister Jean, Schmidt received international attention and acclaim during the Loyola Ramblers' appearance during the 2018 NCAA March Madness tournament, the year she served as the team's chaplain at age 98.

Tom Hitcho, Loyola senior associate athletics director and longtime friend of Sr. Jean Schmidt, was the first to sit next to the statue after it was unveiled Aug. 21, 2026, at Loyola University Chicago. (Courtesy of Loyola University Chicago)

But during the statue unveiling ceremony, university officials and members of her congregation, the Sisters of Charity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, praised Schmidt for being more than a dedicated basketball fan. "Sister Jean's ministry of presence was a gift to generations of Ramblers," said Loyola President Mark Reed, who praised Schmidt's compassion, joy and concern and care for students and staff. In her remarks, Sr. LaDonna Manternach, president of the Sisters of Charity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, recalled Schmidt's love of Loyola students. "A good listener, she inspired many to pursue their dreams with purpose. Her deep trust in God guided her life and encouraged others to trust their own journey. "

एक हजार स बेसी मृतक आ 4500 स बेसी लापता भेला स कैरिटास नेपाल क कार्यकारी निदेशक चेतावनी द रहल छथि जे 26 अगस्त कए देश मे भारी बाढ़ि स भेल आपदा पूरा नहि भेल अछि आ आगामी महीनो तक अंतरराष्ट्रीय सहयोग क जरूरत पड़त। नेपाल सरकार के खोज, बचाव आरू राहत के प्रयास के बारे म॑ २०२३ स॑ क्लूनी केरऽ सेंट जोसेफ केरऽ सिस्टर्स केरऽ सदस्य आरू कैरिटास नेपाल केरऽ प्रमुख सीनियर सेसिलिया दुर्गा श्रेष्ठ न॑ कहलकै कि स्थिति अत्यंत चिंताजनक बनलऽ छै, आरू हताहतऽ के संख्या बढ़ी रहलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि खोज-बचाव केरऽ काम अखनी भी जारी छै । चीन के साथ हिमालयी राष्ट्र के सीमा के पास नुवाकोट मँ समुदायौ मँ बहलौ बाढ़ के बारे मँ विशेष रूप सँ बात करतें हुअय श्रेष्ठ नँ जीएसआर क बतैलकै कि हजारों लोग प्रभावित होय गेलौ छै, जेकरा मँ बहुत लोगौ के जान गेलौ छै, लोग अभी भी लापता छै, आरू घर, सड़क, पुल, आजीविका आरू अन्य आवश्यक बुनियादी ढाँचा क काफी नुकसान पहुँचैलौ गेलौ छै ।

क्लुनी के सेंट जोसेफ के सिस्टर्स के सदस्य सीनियर सेसिलिया दुर्गा श्रेष्ठ 2023 स कैरिटास नेपाल के कार्यकारी निदेशक के रूप में कार्यरत छैथ।(कैरिटास नेपाल के सौजन्य स)

श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, आपदा के दोसर दिन सं कैरिटास नेपाल आ ओकर साझेदार प्रभावित समुदाय के संग जमीन पर अछि। श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, हम खाद्य आ गैर खाद्य सामग्री, आवश्यक घरेलू बर्तन, आ अन्य आपातकालीन सामान उपलब्ध करा रहल छी। "हम शोक आरू अंतिम संस्कार के संस्कार लेली जरूरी आवश्यक सामान के साथ परिवार के सदस्यौ क गंवा चुकलौ लोगौ के साथ भी सहयोग करी रहलौ छियै, साथ ही अलग-अलग स्थान प प्रभावित समुदायौ क मेडिकल किट भी उपलब्ध करौ रहलौ छियै।" मुदा वर्तमान मे सब सं जरूरी जरूरतक मे अस्थायी आश्रय, मलबा निकासी, आवश्यक घरेलू सामान, बच्चाक कें लेल अस्थायी सीखय कें केंद्र, मनोसामाजिक परामर्श, चिकित्सा सहायता आ बुनियादी आजीविका आ सेवाक कें बहाल करय कें लेल सहायता शामिल छै. श्रेष्ठ आगामी महिनामे अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय समुदायके प्रभावित समुदायके साथ जारी राखैके आवश्यकतापर जोड देलक । हुनी कहलकै कि आर्थिक सहायता विशेष रूप स॑ मूल्यवान होतै ताकि हम्मं॑ तत्काल मानवीय जरूरत आरू प्रभावित परिवार आरू समुदाय केरऽ दीर्घकालिक वसूली आरू पुनर्निर्माण दूनू के जवाब द॑ सकियै । नेपालक जनसंख्या ३.१ करोड़ अछि आ हिन्दू प्रमुख अछि, मात्र लगभग १०,००० रोमन कैथोलिक अछि । लेकिन श्रेष्ठ न॑ कहलकै कि कैरिटास केरऽ प्रतिक्रिया ई छै कि “जमीन स॑ प्रभावित लोगऽ क॑ मदद करै के हाथ” बढ़ाबै के छै, चाहे वू धार्मिक संबद्धता के कोय भी होय ।

संबंधित : नेपालक बाढ़ि मे 'किछु नहि' छोड़ि गेल अछि, कारण कैथोलिक नन सभ सहायता जुटा रहल छथि

लोयोला विश्वविद्यालय न॑ कैंपस केरऽ मूर्ति स॑ स्वर्गीय सीनियर जीन श्मिट क॑ सम्मानित करलकै लोयोला यूनिवर्सिटी शिकागो न॑ अपनऽ एगो आइकन, स्वर्गीय सीनियर जीन डोलोरेस श्मिट — लंबा समय स॑ लोयोला रैम्बल्स केरऽ बास्केटबॉल प्रशंसक, टीम केरऽ चपरासी आरू कैंपस फिक्सचर — क॑ विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ रोजर्स पार्क परिसर म॑ एगो मूर्ति के साथ सम्मानित करलकै । 21 अगस्त कए कास्ट कांस्य मूर्ति क अनावरण, जाहि मे श्मिट कए बेंच पर बैसल आ लोयोला बास्केटबॉल पकड़ने देखाउल गेल अछि, जे प्रिय बहिन क 107म जन्मदिन आ 9 अक्टूबर 2025 कए 106 साल क उम्र मे श्मिट क निधन क एक साल स किछु कम समय पर पड़ल 2018 एनसीएए मार्च मैडनेस टूर्नामेंट के दौरान लोयोला रैम्बलर्स केरऽ उपस्थिति के दौरान ध्यान आरू प्रशंसा, जेकरा म॑ हुनी 98 साल के उम्र म॑ टीम केरऽ चपरासी के रूप म॑ काम करलकै ।

लोयोला केरऽ सीनियर एसोसिएट एथलेटिक्स डायरेक्टर आरू सीनियर जीन श्मिट केरऽ लंबा समय स॑ दोस्त टॉम हित्चो न॑ २१ अगस्त २०२६ क॑ लोयोला यूनिवर्सिटी शिकागो म॑ एकरऽ अनावरण के बाद सबसें पहलऽ मूर्ति के बगल म॑ बैठलऽ छेलै । (लोयोला विश्वविद्यालय शिकागो के सौजन्य)

लेकिन मूर्ति के अनावरण समारोह के दौरान विश्वविद्यालय के अधिकारी आरू हुनकऽ मंडली के सदस्य, सिस्टर्स ऑफ चैरिटी ऑफ द ब्लेसड वर्जिन मैरी न॑ श्मिट के प्रशंसा करलकै कि हुनी एगो समर्पित बास्केटबॉल प्रशंसक स॑ भी अधिक छै । लोयोला केरऽ अध्यक्ष मार्क रीड न॑ कहलकै कि सिस्टर जीन केरऽ उपस्थिति मंत्रालय रैम्बलर केरऽ पीढ़ी लेली एगो उपहार छेलै, जेकरा न॑ श्मिट केरऽ करुणा, खुशी आरू चिंता आरू छात्र आरू कर्मचारी केरऽ देखभाल के प्रशंसा करलकै । अपनऽ टिप्पणी म॑ सिस्टर्स ऑफ चैरिटी ऑफ द ब्लेसड वर्जिन मैरी केरऽ अध्यक्ष सीनियर लाडोना मंटरनच न॑ श्मिट केरऽ लोयोला केरऽ छात्रऽ के प्रति प्रेम के याद करलकै । "एकटा नीक श्रोता, ओ बहुतो केँ अपन सपना केँ उद्देश्य सँ पूरा करबाक लेल प्रेरित केलनि। भगवान पर हुनकर गहींर भरोसा हुनकर जीवन केँ मार्गदर्शन केलक आ दोसरो केँ अपन यात्रा पर भरोसा करबाक लेल प्रोत्साहित केलक।"

title: Nepal floods: Death toll climbs to 1,355 as rescue efforts continue; nearly 5,000 still missing - The Hindu
description: Nepal floods: Death toll climbs to 1,355 as rescue efforts continue; nearly 5,000 still missing  The Hindu
publisher.title: The Hindu
full_article:
The death toll from the devastating flash floods in Nepal surged to 1,355 on Monday (September 7, 2026) as more bodies were recovered from the affected areas, authorities said.

Rescue teams continued to search for 4,996 people, including at least 589 foreign nationals, who remain missing, while 13,396 people have been rescued so far, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) said.

Nepal flash floods: Death toll rises to 1,344

According to NDRRMA, 363 bodies have been recovered from Chitwan district, 221 from Nawalparasi West, 222 from Nawalparasi East and 197 from Nuwakot.

Similarly, 169 bodies were recovered from Rasuwa, 75 from Gorkha, 70 from Dhading and 38 from Tanahu, it said.

The joint command of security forces is actively conducting search and rescue operations.

Major rescue operations are underway at hydropower projects in flood-affected districts, where hundreds of men are believed to be trapped in tunnels. Teams of experts from India and China are assisting their Nepali counterparts in these operations.

The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal.

Nepal flash floods 2026 Nepal observes national mourning on 13th day of flash flood tragedy

Nepal flood survivors join rescue and relief operations as they grieve, search for their loved ones

How a mountain collapse triggered Nepal’s deadly flood in just 7 minutes | The Climate Economy

Nepal floods: DNA testing offers last hope to families searching for missing loved ones

The Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border region, carried the floodwaters downstream, sweeping away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects.

The disaster also killed at least 21 people on the Chinese side, while more than 500 people remain missing in Tibet, according to Chinese media reports.

title: Nepal mourns flood victims as hopes persist for workers trapped in tunnels - TRT World
description: Nepal mourns flood victims as hopes persist for workers trapped in tunnels  TRT World
publisher.title: TRT World
full_article:
Nepal held a national day of mourning on Monday for victims of devastating glacial floods, as families of missing hydropower workers feared trapped in tunnels prayed rescuers might yet find them alive.

The August 26 glacial and mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border killed at least 1,398 people, with more than 5,500 missing, including around 800 foreigners.

Flags flew at half-mast, with candlelight vigils planned later in the day, following traditional Hindu mourning rituals on the 13th day after death.

Hundreds of hydropower workers are among the missing, but the rescue of three of them from deep inside tunnels, two Nepalis on Friday and a Chinese man on Saturday, have buoyed hopes that more could still be alive.

Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP on Monday that rescue efforts were continuing "with the same tempo we had on day one".

"Our focus is on search and rescue at three levels, on ground, by air, and in the tunnels," he said.

"We are making sure that no one is still stranded."

Entire communities have been swept away, roads destroyed, and homes demolished.

'Hope'

But families of some of the missing workers who gathered in the capital Kathmandu said the government must move faster.

"We have a lot of hope," said Reena Amatya Shrestha, whose brother is among the missing.

"They say they are doing rescue. If the rescue is there, where's the result? We need the result."

Related TRT World - Rescuers pull Chinese national alive from Nepal tunnel after 10 days

Australian tunnel rescue expert Arnold Dix, who is advising Nepali teams, said the operation presented an unprecedented challenge.

"We are facing something I have never faced before," said Dix, president of the International Tunnelling and Underground Space Association, in a post on social media.

"Not one rescue, but multiple potential rescues, unfolding at the same time, in different places, each with its own dangers, uncertainties, and lives that may still be saved."

नेपाल सेना के प्रवक्ता राजा राम बस्नेट सोमदिन एएफपी के कहलनि जे, बचाव के प्रयास जारी अछि, जेना पहिल दिन छल।

ओ कहला जे हमर ध्यान तीन स्तर पर, जमीन पर, हवाई मार्ग स आ सुरंग मे खोज आ बचाव पर अछि।

"हम सब ई सुनिश्चित क' रहल छी जे एखनो कियो फंसल नहि अछि।"

पूरा समुदाय बहल अछि, सड़क तबाह भ गेल अछि, आ घर तोड़ि देल गेल अछि।

'आशा'।

title: Some Nepal villages so devastated, you’d think they never existed, says Malaysian relief volunteer - Yahoo
description: Some Nepal villages so devastated, you’d think they never existed, says Malaysian relief volunteer  Yahoo
publisher.title: Yahoo
full_article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Some villages in Nepal have been so completely devastated by the floods that there is no sign they ever existed, according to Malaysian relief volunteers who have seen the destruction first-hand.

Mercy Malaysia Rapid Assessment Team leader Vivegananthan Rajangam said some settlements along the rivers were left without a single house after the floods tore through Benighat, Nuwakot and Bidur.

"The damage is very severe. In some villages, there isn't even one house left. If someone went there for the first time, they would think there was no village there," he told Harian Metro today.

"In many places hit by the floods along the river, nobody lives there anymore. In some places, there is no trace of any houses at all."

Even concrete buildings were not spared, with only about 20 per cent of such structures still standing in some settlements, he said.

"Most of these concrete buildings were also swept away," Vivegananthan recounted.

Survivors have since been moved away from the worst-hit areas, with many evacuated to Kathmandu and Nuwakot and housed in schools and halls on higher ground.

Vivegananthan said the Nepali authorities had also set up temporary shelters for those who survived the floods.

In Nuwakot alone, 19 such shelters have been established, he said.

Based on discussions with local authorities and assessments on the ground, food supplies at the shelters were adequate, but survivors needed other forms of assistance.

Mercy Malaysia's three-member team will remain in Nepal for about 10 days to assess how best to support those who survived the disaster.

Vivegananthan stressed that the team was not involved in search and rescue operations but was focused on helping survivors rebuild their lives.

"We are not involved in search and rescue. We are here to help those who survived," he said.

Among the assistance provided are medicines, cooking equipment and toys for children, which are being channelled through Nepali authorities, including the country's Health Ministry.

"The assistance we provide is aimed at helping them continue their lives as best as possible so they can return to normal," Vivegananthan said.

title: Virginia group raises money and awareness for Nepal after catastrophic flooding - WTOP News
description: Virginia group raises money and awareness for Nepal after catastrophic flooding  WTOP News
publisher.title: WTOP News
full_article:
Eleven days after catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-China border killed more than 1,300 people and left thousands missing, hundreds of workers are still believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites buried by mudslides.

Former Haymarket Town Council member Madhu Panthi and the Manassas-based America Nepal Helping Society are asking for support.

“In the world, I’d like to humbly request if there is any equipment that can dig and to open the tunnel … you know more than 5,000 people are missing. And what is the best mechanism to save their life? That’s what we are looking for,” Panthi said.

Panthi moved to Northern Virginia from Nepal in 2001 and helped coordinate donations and disaster response efforts after a 7.8 magnitude earthquake killed thousands and damaged more than 1 million homes and buildings in Nepal in 2015.

“That earthquake also did lots of damage. But earthquake, you can remove the debris and you can find the people in there. But this one is, you know, wiping out everything, and now the roads are not there. The bridges are not there. House, school and everything, everything is destroyed and wiped away,” Panthi said

The nonprofit has set an initial goal of raising $100,000 to support emergency shelter, food, water, health services and other relief efforts. As of Sunday, it had raised more than $52,000.

Panthi said the group is working with the Embassy of Nepal in D.C. and the Nepalese government, to help determine where the money is needed most.

According to the organization’s website, all donations are “subject to due diligence and final approval” and that the money “may support Government of Nepal disaster-relief funds identified in the Government’s 26 August appeal and/or other qualified humanitarian recipients.”

“They can donate by credit card. They can send by check. And all money goes 100% to the victims of Nepal: their food, their shelter, their medical, you know, their clothes, their livelihood,” Panthi said.

Panthi, who said one of his closest friends remains among the missing, told WTOP that ANHS is not sending rescue teams to the disaster area, unlike after Nepal’s 2015 earthquake when some of the group’s members went to distribute aid alongside Fairfax County Fire and Rescue personnel deployed with USAID’s Disaster Assistance Response Team.

Instead, the group is focused on raising money and working within Nepal’s “one door policy,” which is intended to streamline relief distribution and prevent aid from being unevenly distributed. “We don’t want to, you know, send somebody and then some area-people are not getting [help], and some area-people have too much,” Panthi said.

Panthi said that’s another reason ANHS is so focused on its financial goal to help Nepal: “Our heart, our brain, our everything is there. Our family are there. What can we do?”

Last week, PKP Tender Hearts Foundation, an area group dedicated to preserving Nepalese culture and serving communities in Nepal, held a candlelight vigil in Fairfax County with the George Mason University’s Nepalese Student Association to raise money and awareness for the flood victims.

People interested in donating to the America Nepal Helping Society’s disaster relief fund can do so through the organization’s website.

गैर-लाभकारी संगठन न॑ आपातकालीन आश्रय, भोजन, पानी, स्वास्थ्य सेवा आरू अन्य राहत प्रयासऽ म॑ सहायता लेली एक लाख डॉलर जुटाबै के प्रारंभिक लक्ष्य तय करल॑ छै । रविदिन तक एहि स 52 हजार डॉलर स बेसी क राशि जुटा चुकल छल।

पंथी कहलनि जे, समूह डी.सी.मे नेपालक दूतावास आ नेपाल सरकारक संग मिलिकय, ई निर्धारित करबा मे मदद क’ रहल अछि जे एहि पाइक बेसी आवश्यकता कतय अछि।

संगठन केरऽ वेबसाइट के अनुसार, सब दान “यथोचित परिश्रम आरू अंतिम मंजूरी के अधीन” छै आरू ई पैसा “सरकार केरऽ २६ अगस्त केरऽ अपील म॑ चिन्हित नेपाल सरकार केरऽ आपदा-राहत कोष आरू/या अन्य योग्य मानवीय प्राप्तकर्ता केरऽ समर्थन करी सकै छै ।”

"क्रेडिट कार्डसँ दान दऽ सकैए। चेकसँ पठा सकैए। आ सभटा पाइ शत-प्रतिशत नेपालक पीड़ितकेँ जाइत अछि: ओकर भोजन, ओकर आवास, ओकर मेडिकल, अहाँकेँ बुझल अछि, ओकर कपड़ा, ओकर रोजी-रोटी।'

पंथी, जे कहलकै कि हुनकऽ एगो करीबी दोस्त लापता लोगऽ म॑ शामिल छै, न॑ डब्ल्यूटीओपी क॑ बतैलकै कि एएनएचएस आपदा क्षेत्र म॑ बचाव दल नै भेज॑ रहलऽ छै, जेना कि नेपाल म॑ २०१५ केरऽ भूकंप के बाद समूह केरऽ कुछ सदस्य यूएसएआईडी केरऽ आपदा सहायता प्रतिक्रिया टीम के साथ तैनात फेयरफैक्स काउंटी फायर एंड रेस्क्यू कर्मी के साथ सहायता वितरित करै लेली गेलऽ छेलै ।

बल्कि ई समूह पैसा जुटाबै आरू नेपाल केरऽ “एक दरवाजा नीति” के भीतर काम करै प॑ केंद्रित छै, जेकरऽ उद्देश्य राहत वितरण क॑ सुव्यवस्थित करै आरू सहायता केरऽ असमान वितरण नै होय छै । पंथी कहलनि, “हमरा लोकनि नहि चाहैत छी, अहाँ केँ बुझल अछि, ककरो पठाबी आ तखन किछु एरिया-लोक केँ [मदद] नहि भेटि रहल छैक, आ किछु एरिया-लोक केँ बेसी छैक.”

पंथी कहलनि जे, एएनएचएस नेपाल के मदद के लेल अपन आर्थिक लक्ष्य पर एतेक ध्यान केंद्रित करबाक एकटा आओर कारण अछि: “हमर दिल, हमर दिमाग, हमर सब किछु अछि. हमर परिवार ओतय अछि. हम सब की क’ सकैत छी?”

पिछला सप्ताह नेपाली संस्कृति के संरक्षण आ नेपाल के समुदाय के सेवा के लेल समर्पित क्षेत्रीय समूह पीकेपी टेंडर हार्टस फाउंडेशन जॉर्ज मेसन विश्वविद्यालय के नेपाली छात्र संघ के संग फेयरफैक्स काउंटी में मोमबत्ती के रोशनी में जागरण क बाढ़ पीड़ित के लेल पैसा आ जागरूकता पैदा केलक।

अमेरिका नेपाल हेल्पिंग सोसाइटी के आपदा राहत कोष में दान देबय के इच्छुक लोक संस्था के वेबसाइट के माध्यम सं दान क सकय छथिन्ह.

एहि ठाम साइन अप करि अपन ईमेल इनबॉक्स मे ब्रेकिंग न्यूज आओर दैनिक हेडलाइन पहुंचाउ.

title: China Falls Victim To Own Secrecy After Nepal’s Deadly Floods - Newsweek
description: China Falls Victim To Own Secrecy After Nepal’s Deadly Floods  Newsweek
publisher.title: Newsweek
full_article:
China finds itself fighting an information war over its strategic interests in the Himalayas after last month’s devastating flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border put a spotlight on a major hydropower megaproject near India—over 600 miles away and still shrouded in secrecy.

Flooding triggered by a glacial collapse on August 26 claimed over 1,300 lives and up to four times that are still missing, including dozens of Americans. The U.S. Geological Survey said the Lhenda and Trishuli rivers carried glacial debris—ice, water, boulders and later rubble—approximately 62 miles downslope into central Nepal.

China has no hydropower stations upstream, and its infrastructure projects could have played no part in the ice avalanche, the latest assessments suggest. But China is the main contributor of civil engineering works along the riverbanks, so experts speculate that its bridges, highways and buildings in the valley may have altered the speed and composition of the debris flow.

Read More on World

While China and its neighbor India vie for influence over Nepal, Beijing’s skeptics in New Delhi say the worst disaster of its kind in the Himalayas should serve as a warning about Chinese hydropower plans elsewhere in Tibet and their effects downstream. China is fighting back.

When Disaster Strikes

Preliminary reports aided by satellite imagery said the landslide likely began at an elevation of over 17,000 feet, on the northern slope of the Langtang Lirung mountain in Nepal. The collapsing glacier crashed into the valley floor at such a force that it registered as a magnitude 5.2 earthquake, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

The first images of the torrent of mud and floodwater came from surveillance cameras at China’s Gyirong port, which was washed away in a matter of seconds. The border crossing was the main land route for China’s trade with Nepal.

For those living and working in the path of the floods, what little forewarning there was had come too late. Satellite imagery provided by Planet showed the destruction left behind by the fast-moving floodwater, like a giant scar in the earth.

...

When disaster strikes, Beijing’s first reaction is containment, of the damage but also of information.

Within hours of the flooding, videos filmed by witnesses were censored on Chinese social media apps almost as quickly as they were being uploaded. Only approved state media footage remained, as well as any videos that made it out of China’s Great Firewall.

It took the Chinese government 11 days to permit foreign media to report from the Gyirong border area. Beijing’s intense need for control created an informative vacuum in which unfavorable narratives bloomed.

One widely quoted statement came from Madhav Prasad Chaulagain, the former Nepalese environment minister, who said China had failed to warn Nepal about the floods. The comments made to an Indian broadcaster fed critics for days over Beijing’s alleged reluctance to share hydrological data.

Nepalese officials sought environmental monitoring data from Chinese counterparts—including on glacier-related hazards—three months before the disaster but never received it, Reuters reported.

"The broader lesson for the rest of the world is that China’s censorship and cover-ups should not be dismissed as problems affecting only the Chinese people. Opacity does not stay within national borders. Sooner or later, people elsewhere may also bear the costs," Henry Gao, a professor of law at Singapore Management University, said on X.

"The international community should press China to become more transparent and accountable. But meaningful accountability will remain elusive unless China undertakes fundamental political reform and becomes a democracy," Gao said.

China controls the rivers upstream, and water level information can be considered strategically sensitive. Nepal says it will rebuild an early warning system on its border with China utilizing sensors and cameras, but there’s every chance its neighbor will push back.

After Indian and Nepalese social media users on X said China’s lack of transparency was to blame for the deadly floods, the Chinese embassy in Kathmandu fired back, saying the allegations were designed to disrupt China’s cooperation with Nepal.

Chinese authorities, responding to concerns about an information blackout that could cost lives, said they were already sharing whatever data they had. China’s state broadcaster CCTV said glaciers often move and were difficult to predict before collapse.

...

The Himalayas are warming at twice the global average, experts say, making it vulnerable to environmental catastrophes including landslides and floods.

Last week, the Chinese ambassador to Nepal, Zhang Maoming, shared an op-ed written by a Chinese professor in the government-owned newspaper Rising Nepal Daily , which shifted blame for the disaster onto the West.

"The warming in Nepal and the Tibetan Plateau isn't the result of local emissions—it's the accumulated, centuries-old carbon emissions of the industrialized Global North that are bearing down on a cryosphere both countries depend on for their water security," it said.

The Damage Is Done

China’s leaders know the dangers of a runaway narrative, about a palace coup or the instability of the Communist Party’s rule. Its censorship was only partly to do with not wanting to look bad.

Externally, Beijing would’ve been aware of what the disaster meant for its role as a reliable economic partner to Nepal and other developing countries. Internally, its response would speak to its ability to safely manage the region of Tibet, a source of tension with New Delhi, which has hosted the 14th Dalai Lama in exile in northern India for nearly seven decades.

China’s preference for secrecy, however, could cause the greatest damage to its interests in eastern Tibet, where it’s building the world’s largest dam on a river that sustains tens of millions of lives downstream.

The Medog hydropower project, which began last year and will run into the 2030s, will solidify Chinese control of the Yarlung Tsangpo, the critical freshwater source of the Brahmaputra in India and later the Jamuna in Bangladesh.

Nearly a dozen dams of varying sizes have already been built in the eastern parts of politically sensitive Tibet, a geologically fragile region known for devastating earthquakes in the past.

"The geological danger is only part of the story. China is increasingly transforming its control of the Tibetan Plateau—the source of most of Asia’s major rivers—into strategic leverage," Brahma Chellaney, a professor of strategic studies at the Center for Policy Research, a New Delhi think tank, said in an analysis written before the glacial collapse in Nepal.

"It has built cascades of dams on transboundary rivers, withheld hydrological data during periods of tension, and resisted entering any water-sharing treaty with downstream states. Water has become another instrument of coercive statecraft," Chellaney said.

The Chinese government has invited additional scrutiny of its "project of the century" because it won’t disclose further details about the scale of the super dam.

"A secretive Chinese project in my eyes means it’s hard for anyone to find credible information about it, even in Chinese. That is the case for the now under-construction hydropower mega-project on the Yarlung Tsangpo River in eastern Tibet," Shanghai-based energy analyst David Fishman said in a recent Substack newsletter.

China says the $170 billion dam will generate 60 gigawatts of electricity, three times that of the Three Gorges Dam in central China—the largest hydropower facility in the world.

"Yet for all the fanfare about the project’s ambitious scale, the public knows very little about what kind of facility it even is, never mind details like the construction milestones, power export destinations, effects on the surrounding environment, or expected impact on human populations," Fishman said.

Since the disaster in Nepal, Indian social media users on X and other commentators have described China’s mega dam as a "time bomb" that could threaten India.

China may disagree but its reluctance to share information means it’s letting others control the narrative.

Mutual trust in the contested Himalayas is low, and it’s about to get lower.

चीन हिमालय म॑ अपनऽ सामरिक हित के चलतें सूचना युद्ध लड़ै वाला पाबै छै, कैन्हेंकि पिछला महीना नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा प॑ विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ न॑ भारत के पास एगो बड़ऽ जलविद्युत मेगाप्रोजेक्ट प॑ प्रकाश डाललकै-600 मील स॑ भी अधिक दूर आरू अखनी भी गोपनीयता म॑ लिपटी गेलऽ छै ।

26 अगस्त क॑ हिमनदी केरऽ पतन स॑ शुरू होय वाला बाढ़ म॑ 1300 स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के जान गेलै आरू चारि गुना तलक के जान गेलै जे अखनी तलक लापता छै, जेकरा म॑ दर्जनों अमेरिकी भी शामिल छै । यू.एस.

ताजा आकलन स॑ पता चलै छै कि चीन केरऽ अपस्ट्रीम म॑ कोनो जलविद्युत स्टेशन नै छै, आरू ओकरऽ बुनियादी ढाँचा परियोजना बर्फ केरऽ हिमस्खलन म॑ कोनो भूमिका नै निभाबै सकै छेलै । लेकिन नदी के किनारे सिविल इंजीनियरिंग के काम के मुख्य योगदान चीन छै, ई लेली विशेषज्ञऽ के अनुमान छै कि घाटी म॑ ओकरऽ पुल, राजमार्ग आरू भवनऽ स॑ मलबा के बहाव के गति आरू संरचना म॑ बदलाव आबी गेलऽ होतै ।

दुनिया पर और पढ़ें

चीन आरू ओकरऽ पड़ोसी देश भारत न॑ जहाँ नेपाल प॑ प्रभाव लेली होड़ करै छै, वहीं नई दिल्ली म॑ बीजिंग केरऽ संदेहवादी के कहना छै कि हिमालय म॑ अपनऽ तरह के सबसें खराब आपदा तिब्बत केरऽ अन्य जगहऽ प॑ चीनी जलविद्युत योजना आरू नीचें के ओकरऽ प्रभाव के बारे म॑ चेतावनी के काम करना चाहियऽ । चीन एकर प्रतिकार क रहल अछि।

जखन आपदा अबैत अछि

उपग्रह केरऽ इमेजरी के सहायता स॑ मिललऽ प्रारंभिक रिपोर्ट म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि संभवतः भूस्खलन के शुरुआत १७,००० फीट स॑ भी अधिक ऊंचाई प॑, नेपाल केरऽ लंगटांग लिरुंग पर्वत केरऽ उत्तरी ढलान प॑ होय गेलऽ छै । यू.एस.

कीचड़ आरू बाढ़ केरऽ पानी केरऽ धार केरऽ पहलऽ तस्वीर चीन केरऽ ग्यिरॉंग बंदरगाह प॑ निगरानी कैमरा स॑ मिललऽ छेलै, जे कुछ ही सेकंड म॑ बह॑ गेलऽ छेलै । चीन के नेपाल के संग व्यापार के लेल ई सीमा पार मुख्य स्थल मार्ग छल.

बाढ़िक बाट मे रहनिहार आ काज करयवला लेल जे किछु कम पूर्व चेतावनी छल से बहुत देर सँ आबि गेल छल । प्लैनेट द्वारा उपलब्ध कराय देलऽ गेलऽ उपग्रह केरऽ इमेजरी म॑ तेजी स॑ चलै वाला बाढ़ केरऽ पानी केरऽ पीछू छोड़लऽ गेलऽ विनाश क॑ धरती प॑ एगो विशालकाय निशान के तरह देखालऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

...

जखन आपदा अबैत अछि त बीजिंग के पहिल प्रतिक्रिया अछि रोकथाम, नुकसान के मुदा जानकारी के सेहो.

बाढ़ि के घंटों के भीतर चीनी सोशल मीडिया ऐप पर गवाह द्वारा फिल्मायल गेल वीडियो के लगभग ओतबे जल्दी सेंसर भ गेल जतेक जल्दी अपलोड भ रहल छल. केवल स्वीकृत राज्य मीडिया फुटेज बचल छल, संगहि कोनो एहन वीडियो सेहो जे चीन के ग्रेट फायरवाल सं बाहर निकलल छल.

चीन सरकार क॑ ११ दिन लगलै कि विदेशी मीडिया क॑ ग्योरॉंग सीमावर्ती क्षेत्र स॑ रिपोर्ट करै के अनुमति मिल॑ सक॑ । बीजिंग केरऽ नियंत्रण केरऽ तीव्र जरूरत न॑ एगो जानकारीपूर्ण वैक्यूम पैदा करी देलकै जेकरा म॑ प्रतिकूल कथ्य खिललऽ छेलै ।

एकटा व्यापक उद्धृत बयान नेपालक पूर्व पर्यावरण मंत्री माधव प्रसाद चौलागैन के देल गेल अछि जे चीन नेपाल के बाढ़ि के बारे मे चेताबय मे असफल रहल कहलनि। एकटा भारतीय प्रसारक क॑ देलऽ गेलऽ ई टिप्पणी न॑ बीजिंग केरऽ जलवायु संबंधी आंकड़ा साझा करै म॑ कथित अनिच्छा के चलतें आलोचकऽ क॑ दिन भर पेट भरलकै ।

रायटर केरऽ रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, नेपाली अधिकारी न॑ आपदा स॑ तीन महीना पहल॑ चीनी समकक्षऽ स॑ पर्यावरण निगरानी केरऽ आंकड़ा मँगल॑ छेलै – जेकरा म॑ ग्लेशियर स॑ जुड़लऽ खतरा के बारे म॑ भी शामिल छेलै ।

सिंगापुर मैनेजमेंट यूनिवर्सिटी केरऽ कानून के प्रोफेसर हेनरी गाओ न॑ एक्स प॑ कहलकै कि बाकी दुनिया लेली ई व्यापक सबक ई छै कि चीन केरऽ सेंसरशिप आरू कवर-अप क॑ खाली चीनी लोगऽ क॑ प्रभावित करै वाला समस्या के रूप म॑ खारिज नै करलऽ जाय । अस्पष्टता राष्ट्रीय सीमा के भीतर नै रह॑ छै ।देर सबेर दोसरऽ जगहऽ के लोग भी एकरऽ लागत उठाबै सकै छै ।

गाओ नँ कहलकै, "अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समुदाय क चीन क अधिक पारदर्शी आरू जवाबदेह बनै लेली दबाव डालै के चाही। लेकिन जब तलक चीन मौलिक राजनीतिक सुधार नै करी क लोकतंत्र नै बनतै, तब तलक सार्थक जवाबदेही दुर्लभ रहतै।"

चीन नदी सब पर अपस्ट्रीम पर नियंत्रण रखैत अछि, आ जल स्तर के जानकारी के सामरिक रूप सं संवेदनशील मानल जा सकैत अछि. नेपाल के कहनाय छनि जे चीन के संग अपन सीमा पर सेंसर आओर कैमरा के इस्तेमाल सं अर्ली वार्निंग सिस्टम के फेर सं बनाओत, मुदा ओकर पड़ोसी देश पाछू हटय के पूरा मौका अछि.

एक्स पर भारतीय आरू नेपाली सोशल मीडिया यूजर्स नँ चीन के पारदर्शिता के कमी के कारण घातक बाढ़ के दोषी कहला के बाद काठमांडू मँ चीन के दूतावास नँ जवाबी गोलीबारी करतें कहलकै कि ई आरोप चीन के नेपाल के साथ सहयोग क बाधित करै लेली करलौ गेलौ छै ।

चीनी अधिकारी सब सूचना ब्लैकआउट के चिंता के जवाब दैत कहलनि जे, हुनका लग जे कोनो आंकड़ा अछि ओ पहिने सं साझा क रहल छथि। चीन केरऽ सरकारी प्रसारक सीसीटीवी न॑ कहलकै कि ग्लेशियर अक्सर हिलै छै आरू गिरै स॑ पहल॑ एकरऽ भविष्यवाणी करना मुश्किल छै ।

...

विशेषज्ञऽ के कहना छै कि हिमालय वैश्विक औसत स॑ दू गुना बढ़ी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ हिमालय भूस्खलन आरू बाढ़ सहित पर्यावरणीय प्रलय के शिकार होय रहलऽ छै ।

पिछला सप्ताह नेपाल मे चीन के राजदूत झांग माओमिंग सरकारी स्वामित्व वाला अखबार राइजिंग नेपाल डेली मे चीनी प्रोफेसर के लिखल ओप-एड शेयर केने छलाह, जाहि मे एहि आपदा के दोष पश्चिम पर राखल गेल छल.

ओकरा मँ कहलौ गेलौ छै कि नेपाल आरू तिब्बती पठार मँ गर्मी स्थानीय उत्सर्जन के परिणाम नै छै-ई औद्योगिक ग्लोबल नॉर्थ केरौ संचित, सदियो पुरानौ कार्बन उत्सर्जन छै जे एक क्रायोस्फीयर प असर डालै छै, जेकरा प दोनों देश अपनौ जल सुरक्षा लेली निर्भर छै ।

नुकसान भ गेल अछि

चीन केरऽ नेता सब क॑ भागलऽ कथ्य केरऽ खतरा पता छै, महल म॑ तख्तापलट के बारे म॑ या कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी केरऽ शासन केरऽ अस्थिरता के बारे म॑ । एकरऽ सेंसरशिप केरऽ संबंध खाली कुछ हद तलक खराब नै देखै के इच्छा स॑ छेलै ।

बाहरी रूप स॑ बीजिंग क॑ ई बात के जानकारी होतै कि नेपाल आरू अन्य विकासशील देशऽ लेली एगो विश्वसनीय आर्थिक भागीदार के रूप म॑ अपनऽ भूमिका लेली ई आपदा के की मतलब छै । आंतरिक रूप स॑ एकरऽ प्रतिक्रिया तिब्बत क्षेत्र क॑ सुरक्षित रूप स॑ प्रबंधित करै के ओकरऽ क्षमता के बात करतै, जे नई दिल्ली के साथ तनाव के स्रोत छै, जे लगभग सात दशक स॑ उत्तरी भारत म॑ निर्वासित १४वां दलाई लामा के मेजबानी करी रहलऽ छै ।

हालांकि चीन केरऽ गोपनीयता केरऽ पसंद स॑ पूर्वी तिब्बत म॑ ओकरऽ हित क॑ सबसें जादा नुकसान पहुँचै सकै छै, जहां वू दुनिया केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ बांध एगो ऐसनऽ नदी प॑ बनाबै छै जेकरा स॑ नीचें करोड़ों लोगऽ के जान टिकैलऽ जाय छै ।

पिछला साल शुरू भेल आ 2030 के दशक में चलै वाला मेडोग जलविद्युत परियोजना भारत के ब्रह्मपुत्र आ बाद में बांग्लादेश के जमुना के महत्वपूर्ण मीठ जल स्रोत यारलुंग त्सांगपो पर चीनी नियंत्रण के ठोस बनाओत.

राजनीतिक रूप स॑ संवेदनशील तिब्बत केरऽ पूर्वी भाग म॑ लगभग एक दर्जन अलग-अलग आकार के बांध बनी चुकलऽ छै, जे भूवैज्ञानिक रूप स॑ नाजुक क्षेत्र छेकै जे पूर्व म॑ विनाशकारी भूकंप लेली जानलऽ जाय छै ।

नई दिल्ली केरऽ थिंक टैंक सेंटर फॉर पॉलिसी रिसर्च केरऽ रणनीतिक अध्ययन के प्रोफेसर ब्रह्म चेलानी न॑ नेपाल म॑ हिमनदीय पतन स॑ पहल॑ लिखलऽ गेलऽ एगो विश्लेषण म॑ कहलकै कि भूवैज्ञानिक खतरा कहानी केरऽ एगो हिस्सा ही छै ।

चेलानी नँ कहलकै, "ई सीमा पार के नदी प बांध के झरना बनैलकै, तनाव के दौर मँ जलविज्ञान के आंकड़ा रोकलकै, आरू डाउनस्ट्रीम राज्यौ के साथ जल साझा करै के कोनो भी संधि मँ प्रवेश करै के विरोध करलकै। पानी जबरन राज्य शिल्प के एगो आरू साधन बनी गेलौ छै।"

चीन सरकार न॑ अपनऽ "सदी केरऽ परियोजना" प॑ अतिरिक्त जांच लेली आमंत्रित करलकै, कैन्हेंकि वू सुपर डैम केरऽ पैमाना के बारे म॑ आरू विवरण नै देतै ।

शंघाई स्थित ऊर्जा विश्लेषक डेविड फिशमैन न॑ हाल ही म॑ सबस्टैक न्यूजलेटर म॑ कहलकै कि "हमरऽ नजर म॑ एगो गुप्त चीनी परियोजना के मतलब छै कि एकरा बारे म॑ विश्वसनीय जानकारी मिलना ककरो लेली मुश्किल छै, चीनी भाषा म॑ भी । पूर्वी तिब्बत केरऽ यारलुंग त्सांगपो नदी प॑ अब॑ निर्माणाधीन जलविद्युत मेगा परियोजना लेली भी यही हाल छै ।"

चीन के कहना छै कि 170 अरब डॉलर के ई बांध स॑ 60 गीगावाट बिजली पैदा होतै, जे मध्य चीन केरऽ थ्री गॉर्ज डैम स॑ तीन गुना अधिक छै – जे दुनिया केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ जलविद्युत सुविधा छै ।

फिशमैन न॑ कहलकै कि तभियो ई परियोजना केरऽ महत्वाकांक्षी पैमाना के बारे म॑ जेतना धूमधाम छै, ओकरा लेली जनता क॑ ई बात के बारे म॑ बहुत कम जानकारी छै कि ई केना सुविधा भी छै, निर्माण केरऽ मील के पत्थर, बिजली निर्यात गंतव्य, आसपास के पर्यावरण प॑ पड़ै वाला प्रभाव, या मानव आबादी प॑ अपेक्षित प्रभाव जैसनऽ विवरण के बात क॑ कभियो नै ।

नेपाल केरऽ आपदा के बाद स॑ एक्स प॑ भारतीय सोशल मीडिया यूजर आरू अन्य कमेंटेटर न॑ चीन केरऽ मेगा डैम क॑ एगो “टाइम बम” बतैलकै जेकरा स॑ भारत प॑ खतरा पैदा होय सकै छै ।

चीन एहि बात सं असहमत भ’ सकैत अछि मुदा जानकारी साझा करबा मे ओकर अनिच्छा के मतलब अछि जे ओ दोसर के कथ्य पर नियंत्रण राखय दैत अछि.

प्रतिस्पर्धी हिमालय पर आपसी विश्वास कम अछि, आ ई कम होमय बला अछि.

full_article:
Buddhist monks prepare for a requiem ceremony for the victims of the devastating flash floods that struck Nepal on August 26. (Photo: AP)

The national flags were flown at half-mast at government offices nationwide and Nepali diplomatic missions abroad.

People performed memorial rituals and offered tributes to the deceased. As search and rescue operations remain underway, Nepal did not hold large-scale memorial ceremonies on the national day of mourning. President Ram Chandra Paudel was touring flood-hit areas to survey damage caused by the disaster.

Oil lamps are lit during a requiem ceremony for the victims. (Photo: AP)

The Nepalese Army said that the rescue efforts continue at "the same tempo" to make sure "that no one is still stranded" and are focusing on ground areas, from the air, and inside tunnel systems.

As of Monday morning, the flash flood disaster in the border region between Nepal and China killed 1,385 people and more than 5,500 others still missing.
